sources.title: قانون اصلاح قانون مبارزه با مواد مخدر و الحاق موادي به آن مصوب ۳/۸/۱۳۶۷ مجمع تشخيص مصلحت نظام (Law amending the Anti-Narcotics Law of 3/8/1367 and adding articles to it): all 42 articles and 25 notes, read for substance names; Arts 1 (note), 1, 3, 4, 8, 40 and 41 read verbatim in short passages
sources.publisher: Expediency Discernment Council (مجمع تشخيص مصلحت نظام); signed 'رئيس مجمع تشخيص مصلحت نظام ـ اكبر هاشمي رفسنجاني'. Read on FAOLEX (Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN), whose PDF is a print of the dastour.ir legislation portal page; the print names no operator for dastour.ir, and dastour.ir itself refused WebFetch
sources.version: Final approval 'در تاريخ۱۷/۸/۱۳۷۶' (17 Aban 1376, 8 Nov 1997); print header '9/26/2016 www.dastour.ir/Print/?lid=175711', 13 pages; 42 articles (10, 17, 18 and 35 deleted; 39 and 40 marked added). No 1389 or 1396 text is shown. FAOLEX's record (leap.unep.org) cites Official Journal No. 15590 of 6 September 1998
sources.how: WebFetch, every decisive passage read twice with differently worded prompts and compared by script; a third reading for Art. 40's wording and a one-time check for 22 named terms

2c-x.note: Not named in the Anti-Narcotics Law as amended in 1376. The law's Art. 1 note defines narcotics as the substances in «تصويب نامه راجع به فهرست مواد مخدر مصوب ۱۳۳۸ و اصلاحات بعدي آن» (the 1338 Cabinet resolution on the list of narcotic substances and its later amendments) or those «توسط وزارت بهداشت، درمان و آموزش پزشكي به عنوان مخدر شناخته و اعلام ميگردد» (recognised and announced as narcotic by the Ministry of Health, Treatment and Medical Education). Neither could be read, so absence here does not show the item is uncontrolled in Iran. Lists searched: the Anti-Narcotics Law as amended in 1376 (all 42 articles and 25 notes, read on FAOLEX's copy of a dastour.ir print of 26 Sep 2016) for every substance name, twice, and once more for 22 named terms. Not readable (WebFetch refused every official host): the Cabinet list the law's definition relies on, تصويب‌نامه راجع به فهرست مواد مخدره (1338) and its amendments (qavanin.ir/Law/TreeText/164499; dotic.ir/news/5620; solh.ir); Ministry of Health announcements of substances as narcotic; the 1389 and 1396 amendments of the law; قانون مربوط به مواد روان‌گردان (پسيكوتروپ) (the psychotropic-substances law; dotic.ir/news/5619, arakmu.ac.ir); and any Drug Control Headquarters (dchq.ir) or Food and Drug Administration (fda.gov.ir) list. Draft: the law was read only on FAOLEX's copy of a 2016 print, and the decisive lists were not read.

unsettled: THE OFFICIAL CURRENT LISTS COULD NOT BE READ. The Anti-Narcotics Law's Art. 1 note makes a 'narcotic' any substance in «تصويب نامه راجع به فهرست مواد مخدر مصوب ۱۳۳۸ و اصلاحات بعدي آن» (the 1338 Cabinet resolution on the list of narcotic substances and its later amendments) or «توسط وزارت بهداشت، درمان و آموزش پزشكي به عنوان مخدر شناخته و اعلام ميگردد» (recognised and announced as narcotic by the Ministry of Health). WebFetch refused every official host that carries that list or the current law: qavanin.ir/Law/TreeText/164499 (the 1338 list), qavanin.ir/Law/... and /Law/PrintText/..., rc.majlis.ir/fa/law/show/..., dastour.ir, dotic.ir, rrk.ir (Official Gazette), dchq.ir (Drug Control Headquarters), fda.gov.ir/item/... and irc.fda.gov.ir (Food and Drug Administration), maslahat.ir (Expediency Council), and the university food-and-drug deputies at ajums.ac.ir, tbzmed.ac.ir, arakmu.ac.ir and jums.ac.ir. Private law sites (for example ekhtebar.ir, davoudabadi.ir, solh.ir, law-ir.ir, farasai.com, shenasname.ir) appear in search results under these titles but are not official, so nothing was taken from them. As instructed for this country, every item not named in the law text read is recorded as 'Not found in the lists read'; this does NOT show that the item is uncontrolled in Iran.

Currency. The only text read is the 1376 text (final approval 17/8/1376), as printed from dastour.ir on 26 Sep 2016 and copied by FAOLEX. Search results (law-firm and news sites, not used for facts) point to later amendments: an amendment approved by the Expediency Council in 1389 (2010), which they say added industrial non-medical psychotropics (روان‌گردان‌های صنعتی غیردارویی), and an article (Art. 45) added by Parliament in 1396 (2017). One law-firm page describes the current Art. 8 as covering LSD, ecstasy and crystal, which the 1376 text does not name, so Art. 8 at least has probably changed. Their official texts were not read, so every row is draft and the named rows may be out of date.

Host. FAOLEX is an FAO database, not an Iranian government host; its PDF is a print of a dastour.ir page, and dastour.ir's operator could not be confirmed (the site refused WebFetch). All rows are therefore draft even where the two readings agree, as was done for Nigeria's PLAC and FAOLEX copies.

Generic clause in Art. 8: «و ديگر مشتقات شيميائي مرفين و كوكائين» (and other chemical derivatives of morphine and cocaine). Whether it reaches oxycodone, hydrocodone or buprenorphine (recorded as not found) is not stated in the text; a chemist or lawyer should decide.

Art. 40 (added in 1376) names codeine and methadone, after precursors listed in Tables I and II of the 1988 Convention; the article opens with an intent to convert or produce narcotics. Whether that intent qualifies the codeine and methadone clause is a penal question outside this brief; the rows record only that both are named.

Art. 41 exempts the making, trade, keeping, import, export, use and carriage of 'مواد ممنوع' (prohibited substances) for medical, research and industrial uses with a Ministry of Health permit. It is general, so medical_use is null throughout.
Glosses: بنگ is glossed 'bhang' (cannabis herb) and چرس 'charas' (cannabis resin) by the reader; the law prints no definitions. حشيش and گراس do not occur in the 1376 text.

Also not read: قانون مربوط به مواد روان‌گردان (پسيكوتروپ) (the psychotropic-substances law; titles on dotic.ir and arakmu.ac.ir, both refused); any Drug Control Headquarters resolution or Food and Drug Administration list of narcotic, psychotropic or controlled medicines; the UNODC SHERLOC English PDF 'THE ANTI NARCOTICS LAW OF THE ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN' (client error). To finish Iran, someone with a browser in Iran, or a human reader, needs the 1338 list as amended, the Ministry of Health announcements, the 1389 amendment and the psychotropic-substances law, from qavanin.ir or the Official Gazette.
